description: High-performance io_uring transport for ASP.NET Core Kestrel. Drop-in replacement for the default socket transport. Beats sockets on RPS, CPU efficiency (+48% RPS/CPU%), and tail latency on Linux. Thread-per-core architecture with provided buffer rings, zero-alloc send path, and inline HTTP processing.
releaseNotes:
v2.2.1 — Slot free-list: fixes high-c correctness + unlocks stronger wins
• Fix: per-listener connection-slot allocator now uses a pre-populated free-list
  (Stack<int>) instead of the pre-2.2.1 `connId % MaxConnections` modulo. The
  modulo policy silently aliased connIds to slot indices and overwrote live
  connections' slots once connId count exceeded MaxConnections, orphaning their
  recv/send-loop/fd and producing mass errors at connection counts > MaxConnections.
  Default MaxConnections is now 16384 (was 1024). Slot release is deferred until
  all in-flight CQEs for the closing connection have drained, so the generation
  check correctly rejects stale CQEs instead of misrouting them to a new
  connection that happened to claim the same slot.
• Fix: HandleAccept now soft-rejects (close fd, log warning) when the free-list
  is empty, instead of the previous silent-overwrite. No more orphaning under
  bursts above MaxConnections.

Benchmarks (dotnet/Benchmarks aspnet-gold-lin, 56-core Intel Xeon Gold 6330,
Ubuntu-24.04 kernel 6.8, IOURING_THREAD_COUNT=32, 1-trial-per-cell matrix):
  json c=128:  1.07M RPS vs sockets 1.04M  (+0.7%  RPS, -33% CPU)
  json c=512:  979K  RPS vs sockets 937K   (+4.5%  RPS, -38% CPU)
  json c=1024: 1.08M RPS vs sockets 1.04M  (+3.9%  RPS, -37% CPU)
  json c=2048: 1.04M RPS vs sockets 958K   (+8.8%  RPS, -46% CPU)  *pre-2.2.1: 401K errors*
  plaintext-dual c=1024: 15.45M RPS (+0.9% RPS, -40% CPU)
  plaintext-dual c=2048: 15.06M RPS (-1.3% RPS, -52% CPU) *pre-2.2.1: 719K errors*
  tls-steady-dual c=128:  798K RPS (+13.5% RPS, -41% CPU)
  tls-steady-dual c=1024: 1.21M RPS (+7%    RPS, -35% CPU)
  tls-steady-dual c=2048: 1.22M RPS (+9.5%  RPS, -41% CPU)
  0 errors across all 24 cells (12 scenarios/connection pairs × 2 variants).

Known limitation (unchanged from 2.2.0): bombardier TLS handshake-churn with
`connectionclose=true` still hits an IO-loop livelock after the first close.
This is orthogonal to the slot-collision bug — reproduces at c=1 and with
IOURING_MAX_CONNECTIONS=65536. Deferred; keep-alive workloads (the common
production shape) are unaffected.

v2.2.0 — Stability + correctness + smaller pinned heap; consistently beats sockets
• S0 Correctness fixes (3 latent bugs that caused ~1429 socket errors / 60s @ c=2048
  with v2.1.0 and full death-spiral at higher loads):
  - Accept-channel drop: when bounded accept-channel was full under burst, the new
    connection was created but TryWrite return value was ignored, leaking the conn.
    Now: on TryWrite=false, abort + close cleanly.
  - Multishot recv rearm SQ-full silent loss: SubmitMultishotRecv now returns bool;
    callers add to the recv-retry set on failure. No more silent stop-receiving.
  - CQ-overflow recovery: RecoverFromCqOverflow now routes via UsingMultishotRecv
    flag; previously always used single-shot recv even for buffer-ring connections.
• S1 Skip per-connection pinned recv buffer when buffer ring is active (it's never
  used in that path). Saves ~4 KB POH per connection.
• P1 Default ThreadCount tuning: TC=64 was wildly oversubscribed on 56-core boxes.
  TC=32 (or matching ProcessorCount/2) gives same/better RPS at half the CPU.
• P2 Buffer-ring right-size: ReceiveBufferSize default 4096 -> 2048. Halves the
  per-buffer pinned heap; keep-alive HTTP/1.1 small payloads need ~2 KB.
• S2 Diagnostics: new RecvDiagnostics counters (ENOBUFS, EPIPE, ECONNRESET, accept
  channel drops, recv-retry queue depth/water-mark, async-flush pending). Periodic
  log via LogPoolStatsInterval.
• Result: stable to c=4096+ (zero socket errors, zero bad responses, no death
  spiral). v2.1.0 is broken at c>=256 — v2.2.0 fixes that AND beats sockets.

Benchmarks (json, 56-core Intel Xeon Gold 6330, Azure D64as_v5, kernel 6.8, 3-trial
median, single-load except c=2048 which is dual-load 2x c=1024):

  c=256   patched 781,942 RPS @ 28% CPU  vs sockets 753,172 @ 40% CPU
                  +3.8% RPS, -30% CPU, +48% RPS/CPU%, P99 0.64 vs 0.70 ms, 0 errors
  c=1024  patched 1,068,612 RPS @ 34% CPU vs sockets 1,046,915 @ 51% CPU
                  +2.1% RPS, -33% CPU, +53% RPS/CPU%, P99 5.50 vs 6.41 ms, 0 errors
  c=2048  patched 2,132,290 RPS @ 34% CPU vs sockets 2,037,381 @ 48% CPU
                  +4.7% RPS, -29% CPU, +48% RPS/CPU%, P99 5.74 vs 6.55 ms, 0 errors
  c=4096  patched 1,718,626 RPS @ 33% CPU, P99 3.59 ms, 0 errors (stress validation)

  Pinned heap dropped from 75 MB (v2.1.0 at TC=64) -> 16 MB (4.7x reduction).

v2.0.0 — Architecture overhaul: beats sockets by 15%
• IoUringPipeScheduler: custom PipeScheduler runs all pipe continuations on
  the IO loop thread. Eliminates ThreadPool hops for both recv and send paths.
• Inline HTTP processing: Kestrel HTTP pipeline runs on the IO thread
  (like UnsafePreferInlineScheduling). Zero cross-thread signaling.
• Non-blocking send: IValueTaskSource-based send completion. Send loop yields
  after SQE submit, resumes inline on CQE. Zero-alloc send path.
• Connection slot array: replaces ConcurrentDictionary with O(1) direct index.
• Pre-pinned recv buffer: eliminates per-recv Pin()/Dispose().
• Fix SetSqeFd infinite recursion bug (stack overflow when fd registration fails).
• Coalesced PipeScheduler wakeups: flag-based eventfd dedup.

Benchmark: json scenario, 56-core Intel Xeon Gold 6330, kernel 6.8.0
  256c: 2,043K RPS (+9% vs sockets)
  512c: 2,499K RPS (+13% vs sockets)
  1024c: 2,829K RPS (+15% vs sockets)
  CPU usage: 50% (sockets: 90%) — 1.9x more efficient per CPU cycle
  Lock contention: 50/s (sockets: 1,994/s)
  GC time: 0% | Allocation rate: 3.8M B/s (below sockets)

v1.2.0 — Re-enable buffer ring + SQPOLL mode
• Re-enable provided buffer ring (multishot recv) — stalling bug fixed
  on kernel 6.6+. Eliminates per-recv Pin()/Dispose() overhead.
  Controlled via EnableBufferRing option (default: true).
• Add SQPOLL mode support (EnableSqPoll option). Kernel polls the SQ ring,
  eliminating io_uring_enter syscalls. Requires CAP_SYS_NICE or root.
• Ring constructor now accepts setup flags for SQPOLL and future kernel features.
• BufferRingSize option for tuning buffer ring depth (default: 256).

v1.1.0 — Performance: lock-free send path
• Send operations are now enqueued to the IO loop via ConcurrentQueue + eventfd
  instead of acquiring SubmitLock per send. Eliminates 90K+/s lock contentions
  on multi-core machines.
• IO loop is now the sole SQ producer — all submissions are batched into a
  single io_uring_enter per loop iteration.
• Reduces per-send syscalls from 1 each to 0 (batched with recv/accept work).

v1.0.1 — Bug fix
• Fix IOSQE_BUFFER_SELECT constant: was 1<<3 (0x08), now 1<<5 (0x20)
  Matches kernel definition. Fixes EFAULT when using buffer rings with recv.
• Add test project with 10 tests (unit + integration)
• Add InternalsVisibleTo for test project

v1.0.0 — Initial release
• Drop-in io_uring transport via UseIoUring()
• Multishot recv with buffer rings
• Zero-copy send (SEND_ZC)
• Registered file descriptors
• Targets net8.0, net9.0, net10.0
